title: Support for .NET Framework 4, 4.5 and 4.5.1 ends
impact: Machines must have .NET Framework 4.5.2 or later installed to keep getting security updates for 4.x apps

title: Support for Windows 8 ends (Windows 8.1 stays supported)
impact: PCs still on Windows 8 get no more security updates until they are updated to Windows 8.1

title: Extended support for SQL Server 2005 ends
impact: Databases still on 2005 get no more security updates and must move to a newer version, retesting app SQL

title: Extended support for Visual Studio 2005 ends
impact: The Visual Studio 2005 IDE gets no more fixes, so teams still building with it are on an unsupported toolchain unless they upgrade

title: SQL Server 2016 becomes generally available
impact: JSON functions, STRING_SPLIT, DROP IF EXISTS, temporal tables and Always Encrypted become usable on databases moved to 2016

title: SQL Server 2016 becomes generally available with extended support scheduled to end in July 2026
impact: Databases moved to SQL Server 2016 have a known end date, so the next database upgrade and retesting of app SQL can be planned

title: Windows Server 2016 becomes generally available
impact: Containers and Nano Server arrive, and licensing moves to per-core, changing the cost of hosting business apps

title: Windows Server 2016 becomes generally available with extended support scheduled to end in January 2027
impact: Servers moved to 2016 have a known end date, so the next server replacement can be planned
